supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Before round $t$, the learner has the history $h_{t-1}$ consisting of its earlier choices and all feedback and loss information revealed in earlier rounds. It chooses $x_t\in K$ using only $h_{t-1}$ and any learner-private randomization available by that time. The environment supplies a real-valued loss function $f_t:K\to\mathbb R$; it may have fixed $f_t$ before the choice or choose it after the choice, as specified by the environment model, but the learner does not observe $f_t$ before choosing $x_t$.

supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Initialize $W_1(i)=1$ for every $i\in[N]$. At round $t$, set $$x_t(i):=\frac{W_t(i)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}W_t(j)},\qquad i\in[N],$$ draw a measurable expert choice $I_t\in[N]$ with $\mathbb P(I_t=i)=x_t(i)$, and play $I_t$. After observing the whole vector $\ell_t$, update $$W_{t+1}(i):=W_t(i)\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i)),\qquad i\in[N].$$

supplier_excerpts.excerpt: If $D=0$ or $G=0$, set $x_{t+1}=x_t$ at every round. If $D,G>0$, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the metric projection. Set $\eta_t=D/(G\sqrt t)$, put $y_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tg_t$, and set $x_{t+1}=P_K(y_{t+1})$, the unique point of $K$ minimizing Euclidean distance to $y_{t+1}$. Return the decisions $x_1,\ldots,x_T$.
